claims.statement_en: God has helped the believers in many places and on the day of Hunayn, when their great number pleased them but did not avail them at all; the earth, for all its breadth, closed in on them, and then they turned back, retreating.
Then God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers, sent down forces they did not see and punished those who disbelieved; that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
Then, after that, God turns in mercy to whom He wills; God is Forgiving, Merciful.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that on the day of Hunayn the great number of the believers did not avail them, and they turned back [c1]. God then sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers, sent down forces they did not see, and turns in mercy to whom He wills [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
God has helped the believers in many places and on the day of Hunayn, when their great number pleased them but did not avail them at all [c1]. The earth, for all its breadth, closed in on them, and then they turned back, retreating [c1].

Then God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers, sent down forces they did not see and punished those who disbelieved; that is the recompense of the disbelievers [c2]. Then, after that, God turns in mercy to whom He wills; God is Forgiving, Merciful [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat make a contrast between the number that pleased the believers and the help that came from God [c1][c2]. They name what followed the retreat: tranquillity, forces that were not seen, and punishment of those who disbelieved [c2]. The last ayah turns to God's mercy for whom He wills [c3].
chapters.kids_md: On the day of Hunayn the believers were pleased with how many they were, but that did not help them [c1]. God sent calm and forces they could not see, and He is Forgiving, Merciful [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set pride in great numbers beside the help that came from God [c1][c2]. Another is that the passage ends with God's mercy to whom He wills [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how many the believers were, how many their opponents, where the valley or the place was, or the date; the ayat name only the day.
- Not established: who retreated and for how long, or how the forces they did not see acted.
- Not established: what the punishment of those who disbelieved was, or who they were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the opponents, the places and the commanders. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the day of Hunayn, the retreat and what followed. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Hawazin, Thaqif and Taif, and the names of the commanders and the place.
The ayat give no casualties, no dates and no numbers; none are given in this draft.
The chapter on this day in the prophet drafts (content/stories) is separate; this event draft stays inside its own refs.
